findings.en_sentence: The first fossil specimen attributed to Triceratops was found by George Lyman Cannon near Denver, Colorado, in the spring of 1887.
findings.es_sentence: El primer ejemplar fosilizado atribuido a Triceratops fue hallado por George Lyman Cannon cerca de Denver, Colorado, en la primavera de 1887.
findings.problem: Overstates: Cannon's 1887 Denver horns are the first NAMED specimen now attributed to Triceratops; earlier fragmentary fossils (Agathaumas 1872, Polyonax 1874) may also belong to it.
findings.correct: The first named fossil now attributed to Triceratops, a pair of brow horns on a skull roof, was found by George Lyman Cannon near Denver in 1887.
findings.checked_in: enwiki Discovery and identification; F013, F018

findings.en_sentence: While Triceratops was certainly quadrupedal, there is debate regarding its posture, with some believing its front legs sprawled at a considerable angle to support the head's weight.
findings.es_sentence: Aunque Triceratops era indudablemente cuadrúpedo, existe un debate sobre su postura, con algunos creyendo que sus patas delanteras se extendían a un ángulo considerable para soportar el peso de la cabeza.
findings.problem: The sprawling forelimb view was the original, largely abandoned interpretation, not a current position held by 'some'.
findings.correct: Although certainly quadrupedal, its posture has long been debated; originally it was thought the forelimbs sprawled widely to bear the head's weight.

findings.en_sentence: In 1986, John Ostrom and Peter Wellnhofer proposed that all Triceratops remains belong to a single species, T. horridus.
findings.es_sentence: En 1986, John Ostrom y Peter Wellnhofer propusieron que todos los restos de Triceratops pertenecen a una sola especie, T. horridus.
findings.problem: The 1986 single-species proposal is presented alone; the page never says that today two species (T. horridus and T. prorsus) are considered valid, so the reader is left with an outdated picture.
findings.correct: Add that Scannella et al. (2014) supported separating T. horridus and T. prorsus, and both are considered valid today.

findings.en_sentence: Other remains show signs of predation or scavenging by Tyrannosaurus, specifically on the largest specimen, with fractures and puncture wounds on the forelimb bones.
findings.es_sentence: Otros restos muestran signos de depredación o carroñeo por parte de Tyrannosaurus, específicamente en el ejemplar más grande, con fracturas y heridas punzantes en los huesos de la extremidad anterior.
findings.problem: Repeats sentence 18/16 (Tyrannosaurus predation or scavenging on the forelimbs of the largest specimen of the group); 'Other remains' wrongly implies a different find.
findings.correct: Remove; it is the same Newcastle group as the earlier sentence.
findings.checked_in: F049, F104 (same fact from enwiki and eswiki)

findings.en_sentence: Triceratops was a massive animal, reaching lengths of 8 to 9 meters and weighing between 6 and 10 metric tons, though specific specimens like Kelsey measured slightly less at 22 to 24 feet long and approximately 5.4 metric tons.
findings.es_sentence: Triceratops fue un animal de gran envergadura, que alcanzaba longitudes de 8 a 9 metros y pesos comprendidos entre 6 y 10 toneladas métricas, aunque ejemplares concretos como Kelsey medían ligeramente menos, con 22 a 24 pies de longitud y aproximadamente 5,4 toneladas métricas.
findings.problem: Kelsey's measurements are repeated in the next sentence, and 22-24 ft (6.7-7.3 m) is not 'slightly less' than 8-9 m.
findings.correct: Triceratops reached about 8-9 m and 6-10 t; keep Kelsey's figures only in the following sentence.

findings.en_sentence: The fossilized skin of specimen Lane was preserved via a unique process called clay templating, where a bacterial mat formed a clay layer that recorded the skin in positive relief.
findings.es_sentence: La piel fosilizada del ejemplar Lane se conservó mediante un proceso único llamado modelado en arcilla, donde una capa bacteriana formaba una capa de arcilla que registraba la piel en relieve positivo.
findings.problem: 'Unique process' is invented; the source only calls clay templating a form of fossilization, and it has also been described in other dinosaur 'mummies' (e.g. Edmontosaurus).
findings.correct: The skin of the specimen Lane is preserved as a thin clay layer formed from a bacterial mat, a form of fossilization called clay templating.
findings.checked_in: enwiki Skin; F044; knowledge (Sereno et al. 2025)

findings.es_sentence: Triceratops eran herbívoros que se alimentaban principalmente de vegetación de bajo crecimiento, aunque podían derribar plantas más altas utilizando sus cuernos, pico y masa corporal.
findings.problem: Drops the hedging: the source says they 'may have been able' to knock down taller plants; Spanish states it as fact.
findings.correct: ...aunque quizá podían derribar plantas más altas con sus cuernos, su pico y su masa corporal.

findings.en_sentence: A 2020 study described co-ossified tail vertebrae in Triceratops, suggesting the condition arose after one individual stepped on the tail of another.
findings.es_sentence: Un estudio de 2020 describió vértebras de la cola coosificadas en Triceratops, sugiriendo que esta condición surgió después de que un individuo pisara la cola de otro.
findings.problem: Illies and Fowler said the pathology 'could have arisen' from being stepped on; text states the cause as concluded.
findings.correct: ...proposing that the condition could have arisen after one individual accidentally stepped on another's tail.

findings.en_sentence: Researchers suggest it is unlikely that the nipple-like projections on Triceratops feature scales bore bristles, unlike the bristles of Psittacosaurus.
findings.es_sentence: Los investigadores sugieren que es poco probable que las proyecciones similares a los pezones en Triceratops tuvieran cerdas, a diferencia de las encontradas en otros ceratopsios.
findings.problem: Feature scales (and their nipple-like projections) are never introduced on the page; Spanish also drops 'feature scales', leaving 'projections in Triceratops'.
findings.correct: Introduce the large feature scales scattered among the basement scales, then say their central projections probably did not bear bristles.

findings.en_sentence: Thomas Lehman defined the subfamilies in 1990 and diagnosed Triceratops as a ceratopsine, an old name for the group now called Chasmosaurinae, based on several morphological features.
findings.es_sentence: Thomas Lehman definió las subfamilias en 1990 y diagnosticó a Triceratops como un ceratopsino, antiguo nombre del grupo que hoy se llama Chasmosaurinae, basándose en varias características morfológicas.
findings.problem: 'The subfamilies' are never introduced on the page.
findings.correct: Thomas Lehman, defining the two ceratopsid subfamilies in 1990, diagnosed Triceratops as a 'ceratopsine'...

findings.en_sentence: Researchers suggest that the bone in ceratopsian skulls is metaplastic, allowing it to change shape over time.
findings.es_sentence: Los investigadores sugieren que el hueso de los cráneos de los ceratopsios es metaplástico, lo que le permite cambiar de forma con el tiempo.
findings.problem: Metaplastic-bone claim appears in the description with no context; in the source it is an argument in the Torosaurus-as-adult-Triceratops debate.
findings.correct: Place it with the Torosaurus synonymy debate or drop it.

findings.es_sentence: El análisis isotópico sugiere que los ejemplares de Triceratops del Yacimiento Óseo de Darnell probablemente habitaban llanuras de inundación de agua dulce, aunque probablemente no estaban restringidos a un solo entorno.
findings.problem: Proper name translated and truncated (Darnell Triceratops Bonebed); also 'probablemente... aunque probablemente' repetition.
findings.correct: El análisis isotópico sugiere que los Triceratops del Darnell Triceratops Bonebed pudieron habitar llanuras aluviales de agua dulce, aunque seguramente no se limitaban a un solo ambiente.

findings.es_sentence: Un ejemplar concreto llamado Kelsey medía entre 22 y 24 pies de largo, tenía un cráneo de 6,5 pies, se alzaba a 7,5 pies de altura y pesaba aproximadamente 5,4 toneladas métricas.
findings.problem: Imperial units (pies) left in Spanish text (also in the previous and next sentences).
findings.correct: Kelsey medía entre 6,7 y 7,3 m de largo, tenía un cráneo de unos 2 m, alcanzaba unos 2,3 m de altura y pesaba unas 5,4 t.

findings.es_sentence: Otro individuo famoso, Big John, se estimó que medía 26,1 pies de largo y 10 pies de altura.
findings.problem: Broken construction (anacoluthon) plus imperial units.
findings.correct: Se estimó que otro individuo famoso, Big John, medía unos 8 m de largo y 3 m de altura.

findings.es_sentence: Existe un debate en curso sobre la función de la gola y los cuernos de Triceratops, con las visiones tradicionales favoreciendo la defensa contra depredadores e interpretaciones recientes sugiriendo roles en la identificación de especies, el cortejo y las demostraciones de dominancia.
findings.problem: Calqued English absolute gerunds ('con las visiones tradicionales favoreciendo... e interpretaciones recientes sugiriendo'); same in sentence 15 ('con algunos creyendo').
findings.correct: Tradicionalmente se han considerado armas defensivas, mientras que interpretaciones recientes proponen que servían para el reconocimiento de especie, el cortejo y las exhibiciones de dominancia.

findings.es_sentence: La piel fosilizada del ejemplar Lane se conservó mediante un proceso único llamado modelado en arcilla, donde una capa bacteriana formaba una capa de arcilla que registraba la piel en relieve positivo.
findings.problem: 'Bacterial mat' is 'tapete bacteriano', not 'capa bacteriana' (and 'capa... capa' repetition).
findings.correct: ...donde un tapete bacteriano formó una fina capa de arcilla que registró la piel en relieve positivo.

findings.es_sentence: Triceratops eran herbívoros que se alimentaban principalmente de vegetación de bajo crecimiento, aunque podían derribar plantas más altas utilizando sus cuernos, pico y masa corporal.
findings.problem: Missing article and calque 'vegetación de bajo crecimiento' (low-growing).
findings.correct: Los Triceratops eran herbívoros que se alimentaban sobre todo de vegetación baja...

findings.es_sentence: Triceratops se clasifica como un género de dinosaurio ceratopsio de la subfamilia chasmosaurina.
findings.problem: 'subfamilia chasmosaurina' is an awkward adjectival form of the clade name.
findings.correct: Triceratops es un género de dinosaurio ceratopsio de la subfamilia Chasmosaurinae (casmosaurino).

findings.es_sentence: El primer estudio ontogenético extensivo sobre los patrones de crecimiento de Triceratops se publicó en 2006 en la revista Proceedings of the Royal Society.
findings.problem: 'extensivo' is a false friend here; should be 'extenso'.
findings.correct: El primer estudio ontogenético extenso de Triceratops...

findings.en_sentence: The largest known skull, identified as specimen MWC 7584, measured 2.5 meters in length when complete, representing nearly one-third of the animal's total body length.
findings.problem: The largest-skull sentence (MWC 7584, 2.5 m) has no Spanish counterpart.
findings.correct: Add the sentence to the Spanish page.

findings.en_sentence: The jaws ended in a deep, narrow beak thought to be better adapted for stripping and browsing than for biting.
findings.problem: The beak sentence (F113) has no Spanish counterpart, although it comes from eswiki.
findings.correct: Add: Las mandíbulas terminaban en un pico profundo y estrecho...
